QF.id: IV Fixed Income Instruments and Bond Markets_11

question.text: A bond has a dirty price of Rs. 100.65 and accrued interest of Rs. 1.46. What is the clean price?

explanation.text: The Logic: Clean Price = Dirty Price - Accrued Interest = 100.65 - 1.46 = Rs. 99.19. Bonds are quoted at clean price but settled at dirty price (which includes accrued interest). The Trap: Rs. 102.11 adds accrued interest instead of subtracting. The dirty price is always ≥ clean price because it includes the accrued interest component. Cross-Exam Context: Clean vs. dirty price distinction is critical for bond trading and is tested in Series IV. Settlement of bond futures also involves clean price quotation. Distributor's Pro-Tip: When you buy a bond between coupon dates, you pay dirty price (clean + accrued interest). The seller receives compensation for holding the bond since the last coupon date.
